# MauQuota 2.1.0-preview.3

This build fixes the appearance editor crash and reduces repeated Keychain authorization prompts.

## Fixed: Appearance settings crash

- Activates the footer's width constraint only after both views share a common ancestor. The previous early activation could raise an AppKit Auto Layout exception and terminate the menu-bar app.
- Adds a macOS app startup smoke test for the appearance editor, run on both Apple Silicon and Intel release jobs.

## Authentication usability

- Cache the OAuth credential object in memory for one app session after a successful Keychain read.
- Reuse the session copy for periodic quota refreshes, reset-credit requests and diagnostics, instead of repeatedly calling SecItemCopyMatching.
- Update the cache after successful token rotation and clear it after logout.
- Add optional Touch ID at app launch through Apple's LocalAuthentication framework, with macOS account-password fallback. The preference is off by default and can only be disabled after unlocking.
- On an enabled device, a canceled authentication leaves MauQuota locked; unlock can be retried from the menu without repeatedly prompting on its own.
- Add tests for concurrent credential reads, successful and failed reads, token saves, cache invalidation, and Touch ID preference persistence.

## Signing limitation

The downloadable DMGs are still ad-hoc signed. macOS Keychain may still request access permission after an app update because the signing identity is not stable. Touch ID verifies the user's presence within the app but cannot bypass the operating system's code-signing trust decision. Consistent certificate signing is required for a durable cross-version solution.

## Other 2.1.0 improvements

- Native appearance color picker with independent ring and text colors.
- Plus/Pro-aware Codex quota presentation.
- No third-party runtime or UI framework added.

This is a preview release. Stable v2.0.0 remains unchanged.
